1 big thing: "Hypermiling" returns
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

High gas prices are reviving an old pastime: obsessing over your car's gas mileage, Axios' Joann Muller reports.

  • With gas averaging $4.28 nationally, drivers are rediscovering "hypermiling" — squeezing every possible mile out of a tank by laying off the gas and avoiding hard braking.

😨 Hypermiling was all the rage in 2008, the first time $4 gas had Americans staring anxiously at their fuel gauge.

  • But the idea goes back much further: Drivers practiced similar fuel-saving tricks during World War II gas rationing and the 1970s oil shocks.

🛞 How it works: Hypermilers keep their tires properly inflated, accelerate gently, anticipate stoplights, coast whenever possible and religiously obey the speed limit.

  • One Wisconsin man told The New York Times that he's getting 83.2 mpg from a Toyota Prius rated at 52 mpg. Gift link.
  • There's another option: Engaging your car's "Eco" driving mode, if available.

Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🌡️ Hottest summer on record
 
Graphic: NOAA

The contiguous U.S. just experienced both its hottest summer and hottest August on record, Alex Fitzpatrick writes from new NOAA data.

By the numbers: This past summer (June–August) clocked in at an average temperature of 74.4°F. That's 3°F above the 20th-century average.

  • In August alone, the average temperature was 75.6°F — 3.5°F above the historical average.

🥵 Zoom in: "Record-breaking heat extended across much of the Southwest, with Arizona (tied), New Mexico, Utah and Colorado each recording their warmest summer on record," per NOAA.

  • The records were driven in part by notably higher-than-average nighttime temperatures, with many areas experiencing little evening relief.
Data: Copernicus Climate Change Service; Chart: Ben Geman/Axios

🌎 The big picture: Europe's Copernicus service says August was the hottest month on record for Earth as a whole amid human-caused climate change and a turbocharged El Niño, NPR reports.

4. 🐶 1 fun thing: Girl Scout pup treats
 
Photo: Girl Scouts of the USA/AP

Girl Scouts of the USA is rolling out its first cookies for dogs.

  • The blueberry-muffin-flavored cookies, called Patch Pals, will be sold online starting in January.

🍪 Also coming this January: Sparkables, the group's first allergy-friendly cookie.

  • The crunchy oatmeal cookie has chocolate chips and colored sprinkles.
